title: Fix silent fallback to dummy results in results_parser.py
description: results_parser.py falls back to dummy/fabricated result data when FRD parsing fails, with no error raised and no warning surfaced to the engineer. An engineer can receive a plausible-looking displacement/stress result that is completely made up. This must raise ResultProcessingError instead of silently returning fake data.

title: [bug] Overlapping-geometry members lose elements when one side is retyped to U1
description:
building_01a and portal_01 fail CalculiX entirely: 8 integration tests fail with
'ERROR reading *BEAM SECTION: *BEAM SECTION can only be used for beam elements'
naming specific element IDs (e.g. 30, 36, 37, 40, 105 in building_01a).

ROOT CAUSE (traced in unified_calculix_writer.py):
1. mesh_mapper.py's shared-element-assignment fallback (~line 190-210, logged as
   'sharing N elements with another member (overlapping geometry)') lets TWO
   members claim the same element IDs in their respective self.element_sets
   entries when geometry overlaps (e.g. an I-section column embedded in a RECT
   member's span).
2. _identify_and_retype_u1_members() (line 431) retypes ALL of a U1-needing
   member's elem_ids to type 'U1' in the shared self.elements dict, including
   elements it only owns via the sharing fallback — with no check that another
   (non-U1) member also claims that same element ID.
3. _write_elements() (line 624) explicitly skips writing any element whose type
   is now 'U1' ('U1 elements are written individually ... inside _write_sections()
   — skip them here'), deferring their *ELEMENT card to _write_sections().
4. _write_sections() (line 999) iterates domain_model.members in order and has a
   dedup guard (line 1018-1027): if a member's element set intersects
   already_sectioned_elements, the member's ENTIRE section is skipped with a
   'skipping duplicate section' warning.
5. If the non-U1 (RECT) member happens to be processed BEFORE the U1 member in
   domain_model.members order, it claims the shared element ID into
   already_sectioned_elements and writes a *BEAM SECTION, SECTION=RECT ELSET
   that still lists the shared element ID (its element_sets entry was computed
   BEFORE retyping and is never filtered afterward).
6. When the U1 member is processed later, the dedup guard sees the shared
   element already claimed and skips the U1 member's section entirely — so the
   shared element's *ELEMENT card (which only gets written from the U1 path) is
   NEVER emitted anywhere in the file.

Net effect: elements retyped to U1 via sharing end up referenced by a stale RECT
*BEAM SECTION ELSET but are never defined by any *ELEMENT card in the .inp file.
CalculiX rejects the reference.

Confirmed via manual trace on tests/integration data:
- Ran examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc through the CLI,
  inspected generated analysis.inp: elements 30, 36, 37, 40, 105, 106, 107, 108
  are referenced by *ELSET MEMBER_M10/M13/M14/M18(+_ORI1 variants) but do not
  appear in ANY *ELEMENT block (verified by parsing every *ELEMENT block in the
  file with a script — confirmed absent from B31, S3, and all U1_Mxx blocks).
- This predates the most recent commits; reproduced identically on commit
  8f87516 (before the c9l/6al beam-normal and warnings-channel fixes), so it is
  a pre-existing bug, not a regression from this session's earlier work.

REPRODUCE:
  python -m ifc_structural_mechanics.cli analyze \
    examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc --output /tmp/b01a
  (fails with return code 201, BEAM SECTION errors for elements 30/36/37/40/105)

  Also affects portal_01 (4 test failures in
  tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestPortal01ResultsJson).

DESIGN SKETCH (not yet implemented):
Likely fix: when _identify_and_retype_u1_members() retypes a shared element,
either (a) split ownership so the non-U1 member's element_sets entry drops the
now-U1 element before _write_sections() runs, or (b) make the dedup guard in
_write_sections() re-derive already_sectioned_elements from self.elements'
actual current type rather than first-claim-wins, ensuring whichever member
matches the element's final type is the one that writes it. Needs a regression
test using an IFC model with a RECT member and an overlapping I-section member
sharing mesh elements (mirrors building_01a's actual geometry).
close_reason:
Fixed in unified_calculix_writer.py with two changes:
1. _identify_and_retype_u1_members() now strips elements retyped to U1 from
   every non-U1 member's element_sets entry once retyping is complete, so a
   native (RECT/CIRC/etc.) member sharing mesh elements with an overlapping
   U1 (I/T/L/C-section) member no longer references those elements in its own
   *BEAM SECTION ELSET.
2. _write_sections()'s dedup guard for overlapping-geometry members now
   subtracts already-claimed elements from a member's set and writes a
   section for whatever remains, instead of skipping the member's entire
   section on any overlap. This fixes the case where a member sharing only a
   few elements with an earlier-processed member (e.g. the building_01a
   "hub" member sharing elements with 5 other members) was losing ALL of its
   elements, not just the shared ones.

Added regression tests in test_overlapping_member_fallback.py:
- TestU1RetypeStripsSharedElements (2 tests) — exercises the retyping fix
  directly.
- TestSectionDeduplication::test_partial_overlap_writes_remaining_elements —
  exercises the partial-overlap write fix.

Verified against the real building_01a/portal_01 example models:
- portal_01: all 4 previously-failing integration tests now pass.
- building_01a: the original *BEAM SECTION "not a beam element" errors are
  gone; CalculiX now proceeds past input-deck reading into STEP execution.
  It hits a DIFFERENT, unrelated, pre-existing bug there (filed separately as
  eez — CalculiX 'gen3delem: first thickness ... is zero').

Full non-slow suite: 729 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (ziq,
buckling benchmark). No regressions.

title: Warn when a cross-section is approximated with loss of fidelity affecting results
description:
Several section approximations silently change the analysis model and are never reported to the user (no logger.warning on the success path, nothing in result['warnings']):

1. IfcAsymmetricIShapeProfileDef -> averaged to a SYMMETRIC I (properties_extractor.py:586, lines 613-614 average top/bottom flanges; stored as section_type='i'). Asymmetry is lost.
2. The U1 SECTION=GENERAL card forces the product of inertia xi12 to 0.0 (unified_calculix_writer.py:968) and supports no offset/eccentricity. For L (angle) sections the true principal axes are rotated (non-zero product of inertia), so bending about the principal axes is not reproduced.
3. Unknown / unsupported profiles fall back to a default section (properties_extractor.py:486) or default to U1 GENERAL (unified_calculix_writer.py:422). The extraction case logs to logger but nothing reaches result['warnings']; the U1-default case only logs info.

Per project policy, any fundamental limitation that affects analysis results MUST raise a user-visible warning. These do not.
design: Record provenance on the Section at extraction time (e.g. a Section.approximations: List[str] or flags like was_asymmetric / product_of_inertia_dropped / is_default_fallback) so the loss is not forgotten once the profile is reduced to scalars. Then, mirroring _validate_model (api/structural_analysis.py:123), add a post-extraction pass that walks domain_model.members and appends a warning dict (message, severity='warning', entity_type, ccx_id=None, domain_id=member.id, plus ifc_guid) to result['warnings'] for each approximated section. Also emit logger.warning and, optionally, an '** *** SECTION WARNING:' comment in the .inp (same pattern as STABILITY WARNING at writer.py:514) for traceability. Each warning must name the IFC GlobalId and member id. Depends on the warnings-channel fix so the messages are not later overwritten.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Tests written FIRST (one per case): asymmetric-I model, L-section model, and unknown/unsupported-profile model each produce a warning in result['warnings'] naming the offending member/GlobalId.
2. Symmetric sections that are NOT approximated (RECT, CIRC, PIPE, BOX, symmetric I) produce NO such warning.
3. Warning text states the concrete effect (e.g. 'asymmetric I-section approximated as symmetric — section properties and neutral-axis location are approximate').
4. Linters clean; existing tests pass.

title: result[warnings] overwritten after CalculiX run — pre-analysis warnings silently dropped
description:
api/structural_analysis.py:124 does result['warnings'].extend(validation_warnings) to record pre-analysis model-validation warnings. But line 176 then does result['warnings'] = parse_result.get('warnings', []), an ASSIGNMENT that REPLACES the list — discarding every warning accumulated before CalculiX ran (validation warnings, and any future extraction/meshing warnings). The CLI prints result['warnings'] (cli/commands.py:310), so these dropped warnings never reach the user.

This makes the warnings channel unreliable and is a prerequisite for surfacing section-modelling limitation warnings.
design: Change line 176 from assignment to extend (result['warnings'].extend(parse_result.get('warnings', []))). Audit the whole function for any other place that reassigns rather than appends to result['warnings'] or result['errors']. Consider initialising parse-stage warnings into a local then extending once.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Test written FIRST: run the pipeline (or a unit-level harness) where _validate_model produces a warning AND the CalculiX output parse produces a warning; assert BOTH appear in result['warnings'].
2. No code path reassigns result['warnings'] after initialisation; all additions use extend/append.
3. Existing tests pass; linters clean.

title: Beam section normal uses longitudinal axis instead of cross-section orientation
description:
`_get_beam_normal()` (meshing/unified_calculix_writer.py:143) returns `member.local_axis[0]` as the CalculiX beam normal. But `get_1D_orientation()` (ifc/entity_identifier.py:808) builds local_axis as [xAxis, yAxis, zAxis] where xAxis = point2 - point1 = the LONGITUDINAL beam axis, and the real IFC orientation (.Axis) is stored in local_axis[2]. So the returned 'normal' is parallel to the beam axis by construction.

Consequences:
- U1/GENERAL path orthogonalises the normal against the beam axis (writer.py:947), which collapses to ~zero and falls back to a CANONICAL perpendicular (global Y->X->Z), discarding the true IFC orientation.
- Native B31 path has no orthogonalisation and can emit a normal parallel to the axis (degenerate; vertical-column crash class).
- The IFC .Axis vector is exactly what encodes section orientation AND rotation about the longitudinal axis for IfcStructuralCurveMember, so honouring it fixes both off-axis orientation and rotation-on-axis fidelity.

Symmetric sections (circle/square/pipe) are unaffected; directional/asymmetric sections (rectangle, I, T, C) are silently mis-oriented, which can swap strong/weak axis.
design: Fix _get_beam_normal to return a vector PERPENDICULAR to the beam axis, derived from the IFC orientation: prefer local_axis[1] (yAxis) or local_axis[2] (zAxis, from IFC .Axis), orthogonalised against the actual beam axis. The geometry-fallback branch is already correct (it computes a true perpendicular) and should be retained for members with no .Axis. Keep the existing U1 orthogonalisation as a safety net. Note: this honours IfcStructuralCurveMember.Axis; per-profile rotation via IfcParameterizedProfileDef.Position is a separate, rarely-used mechanism for structural members and is out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A regression test is written FIRST and fails against current code: build a CurveMember with a known I-section and a known .Axis (e.g. horizontal beam with web vertical), assert the written *BEAM SECTION line-2 normal is perpendicular to the beam axis AND aligned with the IFC .Axis-derived direction (not a canonical fallback).
2. A second test covers a member whose .Axis is rotated about the longitudinal axis (e.g. section rotated 90 deg) and asserts the written normal rotates accordingly.
3. Both native (RECT) and U1 (GENERAL) section paths produce a normal perpendicular to the beam axis.
4. Existing orientation/section tests still pass; black/isort/flake8/ruff clean.

title: Equation node distance 5m > 1m in test_equation_node_distances_structure
description: tests/integration/test_connection_equations.py::TestConnectionEquations::test_equation_node_distances_structure fails: 'Max equation node distance 5.00m > 1.0m — nodes are too far apart (bad element-to-member mapping?)'. The EQUATION constraints generated in the CalculiX INP file reference nodes that are 5m apart instead of adjacent nodes at the same connection point. This indicates element-to-member mapping is assigning wrong nodes to connection equations. Needs investigation of which model is used and why equation node pairs are so far apart.

title: check_completion_status treats inconclusive output as failure, breaking CalculiX integration
description: OutputParser.check_completion_status() returns (False, 'Unable to determine if operation completed successfully') when no success pattern is found in CalculiX output. This causes AnalysisError to be raised even when CalculiX ran successfully but its output doesn't match any of the four hardcoded SUCCESS_PATTERNS ('ANALYSIS COMPLETED', 'ANALYSIS TERMINATED SUCCESSFULLY', 'SOLUTION CONVERGED', 'STEP COMPLETED'). All integration and validation tests that call CalculiX fail with this error. The fix is to either match CalculiX's actual output strings, or treat inconclusive as success (since return code 0 already indicates success). Affects: test_end_to_end.py, test_building_analysis.py, test_results_json.py, test_cantilever_benchmark.py, test_simply_supported_benchmark.py, test_buckling_benchmark.py.

title: Fix geometry fallback to hardcoded [0,0,0]-[10,0,0] in entity_identifier.py
description: When member geometry cannot be parsed from IFC, entity_identifier.py silently substitutes a hardcoded 10m line at the origin. The model then meshes and analyses with completely wrong geometry, producing wrong results with no warning. Should raise ModelExtractionError with the IFC GUID of the failing member.

title: Add CalculiX execution timeout
description: calculix_runner.py has no timeout on the CalculiX subprocess. A diverging analysis or infinite loop hangs the tool indefinitely with no feedback to the engineer. Should add a configurable timeout (default e.g. 300s) via AnalysisConfig, kill the process on expiry, and raise AnalysisError with a clear message.

title: Add pre-analysis model validation
description: Before meshing, the tool should validate that the extracted domain model is well-conditioned: all members have material and section properties, all members are connected to at least one boundary condition or other member (no floating islands), all loads are attached to members, no duplicate member IDs. Currently a disconnected structure is sent to CalculiX and fails obscurely.

title: Fix convergence detection logic bug in output_parser.py
description: Line 129 of output_parser.py uses 'and' instead of 'or': 'if not completed and "ANALYSIS INTERRUPTED" in output_text'. This means a run that has no completion marker AND no INTERRUPTED marker is treated as converged. Should be 'or', so any missing-completion case triggers a non-convergence warning.

title: Fix hardcoded material fallback: missing material data should error, not default to steel
description: When an IFC member has no material or incomplete mechanical properties, properties_extractor.py silently substitutes steel defaults (E=210 GPa, rho=7850 kg/m3). A concrete slab or timber beam then analyses with completely wrong material properties. Should warn loudly (or error) and require explicit material data, not guess.

title: Fix mesh size default inconsistency: CLI help says 1.0 m, code defaults to 0.1 m
description: The --mesh-size option in commands.py advertises a default of 1.0 m in the help text, but the actual default in the code is 0.1 m. This is confusing and produces unexpectedly fine (slow) meshes without the engineer requesting them. Pick one value, document it consistently, and use it everywhere.

title: Fix multiple load cases: each IfcStructuralLoadCase should map to a separate CalculiX STEP
description: Models with multiple IfcStructuralLoadCase entries (Dead, Live, Wind, Earthquake etc.) currently only get a subset of cases written to the INP. Each load case should produce a separate *STEP in the CalculiX input file so all cases are analysed and their results are tagged by case name. This affects correctness for any real multi-case building model.

title: Improve self-weight / gravity load handling
description: Models without explicit IfcStructuralLoadCase entries rely entirely on self-weight, but the --gravity flag must be passed manually. The library has no way to auto-detect that gravity is the intended load. Consider smarter defaults or detection.

title: Validate linear buckling analysis against published benchmarks
description: The linear_buckling analysis type produces two CalculiX steps (static pre-stress + perturbation buckle) and parses eigenvalue multipliers from the .dat file, but results have not been validated against any published benchmark. Add a validation test.

title: [bug] Overlap resolution scattered across write sites causes double shell sections and DLOAD crashes
description: Follow-up from 51j and eez investigation: _write_sections()'s shell-section branch referenced the raw, unfiltered MEMBER_xxx elset instead of the deduped element set, so overlapping shell members could get covered by two *SHELL SECTION cards. Separately, boundary_condition_handling.py's DLOAD-writing code checked element_set_name not in element_sets (key presence) instead of checking non-emptiness, so a member that legitimately lost all its elements to an overlapping member during resolution still got a *DLOAD card referencing a never-written *ELSET, crashing CalculiX with 'ERROR reading *DLOAD: element set'.
acceptance_criteria: Overlap ownership resolved once via a single source-of-truth method (not re-implemented per write site); no double *SHELL SECTION coverage; DLOAD skips members with empty element sets after resolution; full test suite green.
close_reason:
Fixed in unified_calculix_writer.py and boundary_condition_handling.py:

1. Replaced the ad-hoc overlap dedup logic that had accumulated in
   _write_sections() (from the earlier 51j fix) with a single centralized
   method, _resolve_overlapping_element_sets(), called once in the pipeline
   right after _identify_and_retype_u1_members(). It mutates self.element_sets
   in place so every downstream consumer (raw *ELSET cards, orientation
   grouping, nodal thickness, node-membership registration, section writing)
   sees a consistent, non-overlapping assignment. _write_sections() itself is
   back to its pre-51j simplicity — it just reads the already-resolved sets.

2. Fixed two DLOAD-writing checks in boundary_condition_handling.py
   (lines ~1170, ~1270) that tested `element_set_name not in element_sets`
   (key presence) instead of `not element_sets.get(element_set_name)`
   (non-emptiness). A member losing all its elements to overlap resolution
   still has a (now-empty) dict entry, so the old check let a *DLOAD card
   through referencing an *ELSET that _write_element_sets() never actually
   writes (it skips empty lists) — CalculiX rejected the file with
   "ERROR reading *DLOAD: element set".

Rewrote the unit tests from 51j (TestSectionDeduplication) to target
_resolve_overlapping_element_sets() directly instead of _write_sections(),
plus a new no-overlap sanity test. Fixed a real regression this surfaced:
the interim per-write-site fix used elset names like MEMBER_M1_SHELL, which
broke tests/integration/test_element_member_mapping.py's naive
"MEMBER_" prefix matching (treated the raw and filtered elsets as two
different members' sets, flagging false overlap duplicates) — the
centralized fix no longer introduces any new elset names, so this is moot.

Full suite: 730 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (ziq). Slow suite:
7 failures, all the same still-open eez bug (unrelated gen3delem issue,
confirmed unchanged by these fixes — verified the exact error signature is
identical before and after).

title: [bug] building_01a fails with CalculiX 'gen3delem: first thickness ... is zero'
description:
Discovered while fixing 51j (overlapping-geometry element loss). After that
fix, portal_01's 4 previously-failing integration tests now pass completely,
but building_01a still fails — CalculiX now gets past the *BEAM SECTION
card-reading stage (51j's bug) and fails later, during STEP 1 processing:

  *ERROR in gen3delem: first thickness
        in node            1  of element           30
        is zero

This is a DIFFERENT, unrelated bug — it was previously hidden because ccx
aborted earlier (during input-deck reading) before ever reaching this later
element-expansion phase. Confirmed pre-existing and independent of 51j's fix.

INVESTIGATION SO FAR (inconclusive — needs fresh eyes or CCX source access):
- Programmatically verified NO missing or zero-value *NODAL THICKNESS entries
  anywhere in the generated analysis.inp (checked every S3 element's 3 nodes
  against the *NODAL THICKNESS block — full coverage, all values > 0, no
  duplicates).
- The literal node/element IDs in ccx's error message ("node 1", "element 30")
  do not appear to be literal global IDs from our file:
  - Global node ID 1 is a beam-only node (used by B31 element 1), and the
    project's meshing design deliberately keeps beam and shell nodes disjoint
    (separate point registries in gmsh_geometry.py, see CLAUDE.md) — it
    should be impossible for a shell element to reference node 1.
  - The 30th S3 element in file order (literal ID 170, nodes [226, 279, 79])
    has a valid thickness entry for node 226 (0.25).
  - The 30th element in total file order across all *ELEMENT blocks (literal
    ID 31, a B31 element) has a valid, non-degenerate *BEAM SECTION
    (RECT 0.45 x 0.45).
  So "node 1 of element 30" in ccx's message likely refers to ccx's own
  internal renumbering/array-index scheme (per-type or per-expansion-pass),
  not literal IDs from our .inp — needs correlating against CalculiX source
  (gen3delem / gen3dshell routines) or a minimal, hand-built repro to pin
  down which physical element/node it actually is.

REPRODUCE:
  python -m ifc_structural_mechanics.cli analyze \
    examples/analysis-models/ifcFiles/building_01a.ifc --output /tmp/b01a
  (fails with return code 201 during STEP 1, after 51j's fix is applied)

  Affects tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestBuilding01aResultsJson
  (4 tests, marked @pytest.mark.slow).

NEXT STEPS:
- Try a minimal 2-member repro (one shell member overlapping another, similar
  to building_01a's 2RB3iddKX1KOhkwm7i6S3G member) to narrow down whether the
  overlap-fallback for SurfaceMembers has an analogous issue to what 51j fixed
  for CurveMembers/U1.
- Consider instrumenting/building CalculiX from source with debug prints in
  gen3delem to get the real element/node identity, or bisect the .inp file by
  progressively removing shell members until the error disappears.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-07-03), using CalculiX 2.23 source at
~/rpmbuild/BUILD/calculix-ccx-2.23-build/CalculiX/ccx_2.23/src/gen3delem.f:

gen3delem.f's node-count-determination loop (lines 118-144) filters out
C3D/D/G/E/MASS element types before assigning `numnod`, but does NOT
exclude 'U' (user elements, i.e. our TYPE=U1 beams). When the loop
reaches a U1 element, the local Fortran variable `numnod` is simply left
at whatever value a previously-processed B31/S3/etc. element set it to
(none of the if/elseif branches match a U1 element's lakon string, and
Fortran does not reset locals between iterations). The loop then reads
thicke(1,indexe+j) for j=1..numnod. *BEAM SECTION,SECTION=GENERAL (the
card U1 requires) never populates `thicke` at all -- confirmed in
beamgeneralsections.f lines 367-389, guarded by `if(section.ne.'GENE')`.
So this read is always exactly 0, and gen3delem aborts with "first
thickness in node <j> of element <i> is zero" (j and i here are the
LOCAL node index and CCX's internal element number -- NOT global node
IDs, contrary to earlier investigation notes).

Confirmed with minimal repros (saved under /tmp/ccxrepro during
investigation, not committed): a lone U1 element succeeds; adding ANY
other B31 or S3 element anywhere in the same file crashes, REGARDLESS of
element ID ordering (tested U1 first and U1 second -- both crash). So
this is NOT an ordering/numbering bug fixable from the .inp writer side
-- it depends on stack-garbage state left by unrelated parsing code, and
is unavoidable whenever U1 coexists with any other 1D/2D element.

Confirmed against upstream: github.com/Dhondtguido/CalculiX (official
mirror, commit 6d460bc, 2026-06-19) still has the identical unguarded
filter -- bug is NOT fixed upstream as of this writing.

FIX APPLIED (two parts):
1. patches/calculix-gen3delem-user-element.patch -- one-line CalculiX
   source fix (add `.and.(lakon(i)(1:1).ne.'U')` to the filter).
   Verified by patching+rebuilding CCX 2.23 locally: both minimal repros
   and the full building_01a.inp now pass gen3delem cleanly (building_01a
   then hits a separate, already-documented "matrix found to be
   singular" -- the known mechanism-risk limitation, unrelated to this
   bug and out of scope here).
2. CalculixRunner._raise_if_known_gen3delem_user_element_bug()
   (analysis/calculix_runner.py) detects the "gen3delem...thickness"
   signature + mixed U1/native element types in the .inp and raises a
   clear, actionable AnalysisError instead of the generic CCX message,
   pointing at the patch. Unit tests added in
   tests/unit/analysis/test_calculix_runner.py
   (TestGen3delemUserElementBugDetection).
3. Documented in CLAUDE.md Known Limitations.

Not yet done: submitting the patch upstream to Dhondtguido/CalculiX
(GitHub issue -- repo has issues enabled, 67 open, actively used). Patch
file and repro are ready; needs a human-authorized post since it's a
public external action.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed as a CalculiX 2.23 gen3delem.f bug (missing 'U'-prefix exclusion for USER ELEMENT types); fixed via source patch (patches/calculix-gen3delem-user-element.patch, verified by rebuilding CCX) plus a code-side clear-error detection in CalculixRunner

title: _write_validated_loads_within_step missing elements_data parameter
description: elements_data was added to write_analysis_steps (line 644) to enable U1 DLOAD→CLOAD conversion, but was never forwarded to _write_validated_loads_within_step's parameter list (line 1018). All 3 call sites omit it. The result: the 'if elements_data and ...' branch at line 1174 is always False, so U1 distributed loads are always silently dropped rather than being converted to work-equivalent CLOADs. This also causes flake8/ruff F821 (undefined name) errors.

title: Warn when a directional section is analysed in a default (non-IFC) orientation
description:
When the beam normal cannot be taken from the IFC orientation, the writer silently falls back to a CANONICAL perpendicular (global Y->X->Z) — _get_beam_normal geometry fallback (unified_calculix_writer.py:180-229) and the U1 orthogonalise fallback (writer.py:951-960). For symmetric sections (circle, square, pipe) orientation is immaterial, but for DIRECTIONAL sections (rectangle, I, T, C) a wrong orientation interchanges the strong and weak bending axes — a result-affecting limitation that is currently emitted at most as logger.info, and the orthogonalise fallback is fully silent. Nothing reaches result['warnings'].

This is the user-facing counterpart to the orientation bug (ifc_structural_mechanics-c9l). Even after that fix, members with no usable IFC .Axis will still be placed in a default orientation and the user must be told.
design: When a canonical/default orientation is used for a member whose section is directional (non-axisymmetric — i.e. not circle/pipe/square), append a warning to result['warnings'] naming the member id and IFC GlobalId, and emit logger.warning. Determine 'directional' from section_type and, where needed, Iy != Iz. Route via the same warnings channel as the section-approximation warnings. Should NOT warn for axisymmetric sections or for members whose IFC .Axis was honoured. Depends on the warnings-channel fix; coordinate with c9l so the warning fires only for genuinely missing/ambiguous orientation, not cases the fix now handles.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Test written FIRST: a directional-section member with no usable IFC .Axis produces an orientation warning in result['warnings'] naming the member/GlobalId.
2. An axisymmetric-section member (circle/pipe) in the same situation produces NO warning.
3. A member whose IFC orientation IS honoured produces NO warning.
4. Linters clean; existing tests pass.

title: Native B31 beam-section path lacks beam-normal orthogonalisation safety net
description:
The U1/GENERAL section writer (_write_beam_section_general, meshing/unified_calculix_writer.py:947) orthogonalises the beam normal against the actual beam axis (computed from element node coords) and falls back to a canonical perpendicular if degenerate. The native B31 path (_write_beam_section_for_set, ~writer.py:743) does NOT do this — it writes whatever _get_beam_normal() returns directly on line 2 of the *BEAM SECTION card. If that vector is parallel/near-parallel to the beam axis (which it currently always is for members with an IFC .Axis — see the related bug), CalculiX gets a degenerate local system.

This is defence-in-depth: even after the _get_beam_normal fix, the native path should guarantee the emitted normal is unit-length and perpendicular to the beam axis.
design: Extract the orthogonalise-and-fallback logic from _write_beam_section_general into a shared helper (e.g. _orthogonal_beam_normal(raw_normal, elem_ids)) that computes the beam axis from the first element's node coords, subtracts the parallel component, and falls back to a canonical perpendicular when degenerate. Call it from BOTH the native B31 path and the U1 path so there is a single source of truth.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Test written FIRST: feed a native RECT member a beam normal parallel to its axis and assert the *BEAM SECTION line-2 vector written is unit-length and perpendicular to the beam axis (not parallel).
2. Orthogonalisation logic is shared between native and U1 paths (no duplication).
3. Existing section tests pass; linters clean.

title: Buckling benchmark finds no eigenvalues in .dat file
description:
test_buckling_benchmark.py has two tests. PARTIAL FIX applied:

1. test_buckling_eigenvalue_parsed — NOW PASSES after fix in results_parser.py. CalculiX writes 'B U C K L I N G   F A C T O R   O U T P U T' (spaced letters) but parser checked for 'BUCKLING FACTOR'. Fixed: trigger now matches 'B U C K L I N G' OR 'BUCKLING FACTOR'. Also fixed block termination: was ending on column headers before any data, now only ends after data is collected.

2. test_first_eigenvalue_matches_euler — STILL FAILS. Parsed eigenvalue = 18.71, but Euler analytical P_cr = 1.728e7 N (6 orders of magnitude off). Hypothesis: CalculiX B31 elements are expanded internally to C3D8I solid elements, and the geometric stiffness from this internal representation does not reproduce Euler column buckling accurately at the macro level. The INP uses 10 B31 elements, RECT 0.1x0.1 section, 1N preload along beam axis.

NEXT STEPS: investigate CalculiX B31 buckling behavior — either (a) switch the benchmark to use shell/solid elements (S4R or C3D8) to avoid B31 internal expansion issues, or (b) read CalculiX docs on BUCKLE with B31 to find what eigenvalue it actually produces, or (c) change the test to validate a known-correct CalculiX B31 buckling case.

title: portal_01 shows 0 displacement: U1 element DLOAD not applied
description:
test_results_json.py::TestPortal01ResultsJson::test_displacement_plausible fails because portal_01 uses I-sections → U1 elements, and DLOAD was skipped for U1 elements (CalculiX crash: 'face 2 of 2-node element').

FIX IMPLEMENTED (not yet tested/committed): boundary_condition_handling.py now has _compute_u1_distributed_cloads() which converts a distributed load on a U1 element set to equivalent nodal CLOADs (q*L/2 per node). write_analysis_steps() gains an optional elements_data parameter; when provided and a U1 DLOAD is encountered, it calls _compute_u1_distributed_cloads() and writes a *CLOAD section instead of skipping. unified_calculix_writer.py passes elements_data=dict(self.elements) to write_analysis_steps().

NEXT STEPS: run tests to verify the fix works — pytest tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestPortal01ResultsJson::test_displacement_plausible. Then commit the 3 changed files together.
close_reason: Fixed by elements_data forwarding fix (xld): _write_validated_loads_within_step now receives elements_data so U1 DLOAD→CLOAD conversion runs. All 4 portal_01 tests pass.

title: Extractor raises ModelExtractionError for invalid type but test expects ValueError
description: tests/integration/test_extraction_pipeline.py::TestExtractionPipeline::test_extractor_error_handling passes an integer (123) to Extractor() and expects ValueError. But extractor.py:69 raises ModelExtractionError instead. Fix: either change extractor.py to raise ValueError for invalid input types, or update the test to expect ModelExtractionError.

title: calculix_timeout=600 added to analyze_ifc/run_enhanced_analysis without updating tests
description: run_enhanced_analysis() and analyze_ifc() now pass calculix_timeout=600 in their call signatures, but tests in test_commands.py (TestEnhancedCLICommands.test_analyze_successful, test_analyze_custom_params) and test_structural_analysis.py (test_run_enhanced_analysis_backward_compatibility) use assert_called_once_with() without the calculix_timeout kwarg, so they fail. Fix: update the mock assertions in those tests to include calculix_timeout=600.

title: Write missing unit tests for recent changes
description: Several recent bug fixes and features lack unit test coverage: _validate_model(), loads_extractor GRAVITY group fix, LoadConfiguration averaging, L/T/C section extractors, non-SI unit warning, CLI --timeout.
close_reason: 59 new unit tests written and passing — all 7 coverage gaps addressed

title: Fix IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration: only first load value is used
description: loads_extractor.py line 675-679 reads IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration but only uses the first value from the Values array. Multi-point load distributions (e.g. trapezoidal line loads) are silently truncated to a point load. Should either implement proper interpolated distribution or raise a clear not-implemented warning.

title: Document and stabilise result JSON schema for downstream tools
description: The results JSON written by run_enhanced_analysis() has no documented schema. Keys, units, and structure can change between versions without warning, breaking downstream tools that process the results. Define a versioned schema (e.g. results_v1.json), document it, and add a schema version key to the output. Units should be explicitly stated (SI: metres, Newtons, Pascals).

title: Consolidate duplicate error/convergence detection logic
description: OutputParser (output_parser.py) and ErrorDetector (error_handling.py) independently define the same ~40 CalculiX error patterns and convergence checks. Any fix or new pattern must be applied in two places. Consolidate into a single implementation — OutputParser should delegate to ErrorDetector, or merge into one class.

title: Validate IFC project units and warn on non-SI input
description: The extractor applies unit scale factors but never validates that they are reasonable. A model authored in imperial units (feet, kips) with a missing unit declaration will produce silently wrong results. Should check extracted unit scales against expected SI ranges and warn/error if they look wrong (e.g. length_scale not in [0.001, 1000]).

title: Support I-section beam profiles natively
description: Only rectangular, circular, pipe (hollow circle), and box (hollow rectangle) cross-sections are supported for CalculiX B31 beam elements. I-sections are currently approximated as equivalent rectangles preserving area and second moment of area. Proper CalculiX B31 I-section support should be added.

title: Support partial connection end-releases
description: Connection end-releases read from IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.AppliedCondition are modelled as full pins (all three rotational DOFs released). Partial releases — where only one member or one rotation axis is released — are not yet supported.
close_reason: Per-member per-axis release tracking implemented; writer emits partial EQUATION coupling; 29 new tests

title: Fix overlapping members losing physical group during mesh fragmentation
description: Members with identical or overlapping geometry may lose their physical group assignment during fragment(). Their sections are skipped with a warning; a fallback assigns the nearest elements by spatial proximity. Need a robust fix so physical groups survive fragmentation.
close_reason: Exact-overlap members now share a combined physical group ('A||B'). Writer parses pipe-separated names and assigns elements to all named members. Partial-overlap fallback preserved.

title: Fix connection geometry: use IFC topology instead of proximity search
description: Currently connections are resolved by geometric proximity (0.5 m tolerance) rather than using the IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relationship topology defined in the IFC file. This can cause incorrect connectivity for closely spaced but unconnected members.
close_reason: Replaced 0.5m proximity search with endpoint-targeting: uses domain model geometry to find member endpoint closest to connection position, then matches mesh node within 10mm. Falls back to 0.5m for members without geometry.

title: slab_01 has no loads: displacement envelope always empty
description:
test_results_json.py::TestSlab01ResultsJson::test_member_envelope_present fails because slab_01 uses shell elements. CalculiX *NODAL THICKNESS causes shell expansion: original mesh nodes (e.g. 1-92) are duplicated into expansion nodes (93-368) in the FRD. node_to_member only maps original node IDs → FRD DISP block only contains expansion node IDs → no overlap → per-member displacement attribution fails → no envelope key in results.

FIX IMPLEMENTED (not yet tested/committed): _register_node_memberships() in unified_calculix_writer.py now detects shell members (S3/S4/S6/S8 element types). For those members, after registering original node IDs, it also registers nid+N, nid+2N, nid+3N for all three expansion layers (where N = max_node_id in mesh).

NEXT STEPS: run tests to verify the fix works — pytest tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestSlab01ResultsJson::test_member_envelope_present. Verify N offset matches actual FRD expansion (confirmed via inspection that slab_01 has 92 nodes and FRD contains nodes 93-368 in 3 layers at offsets 92, 184, 276). Then commit the 3 changed files together.
close_reason: Already fixed by commit 539c49c (shell expansion node registration in _register_node_memberships). Verified: tests/integration/test_results_json.py::TestSlab01ResultsJson::test_member_envelope_present passes.

title: Module-level sys.modules stubs break test_gmsh_utils.py collection (fixed) and other tests
description: Seven test files stub ifc_structural_mechanics.meshing.gmsh_utils at module level using 'if not in sys.modules: _stub(...)'. Since tests/unit/api/ sorts before tests/unit/meshing/ alphabetically, test_validate_model.py's stub poisons sys.modules before test_gmsh_utils.py is collected, causing ImportError for GmshExecutableRunner. Partially fixed in test_gmsh_utils.py by adding sys.modules.pop() before the import (same pattern as test_support_point_seeding.py for gmsh_geometry). Root problem: all these module-level stubs are fragile and test-order-dependent. Long-term fix: move stubs into conftest.py fixtures or autouse fixtures scoped to the test session, so ordering doesn't matter. Also affects test_support_point_seeding.py in full-suite runs.

title: Standardise exception handling: use custom exception hierarchy consistently
description: The codebase has a custom exception hierarchy in utils/error_handling.py (ModelExtractionError, MeshingError, AnalysisError, ResultProcessingError) but it is used in only ~30 of ~177 raise sites. The remaining 147 raises use plain ValueError or RuntimeError, meaning callers cannot distinguish mesh failures from parse failures or IFC extraction errors by catching specific types. Additionally, the error_context() context manager in error_handling.py has zero callers despite being written to wrap exceptions with pipeline context. The fix is to audit all raise sites in ifc/, meshing/, and analysis/ and replace plain exceptions with the appropriate custom type, and wire error_context() into the key pipeline stages.

title: Extract MeshMapper and SectionWriter from UnifiedCalculixWriter
description: unified_calculix_writer.py is 2043 lines with 60+ methods handling too many concerns: mesh I/O, three element-to-member mapping strategies, section writing, material writing, connection EQUATION writing, U1 user-element tracking, gravity load pre-computation, and mechanism detection. The element-to-member mapping section (physical groups → spatial → naive fallback) is the most fragile part and has required the most bug fixes (zvo, 4eu, sjk). Extracting a MeshMapper class (owns the three mapping strategies and their selection logic) and a SectionWriter class (owns beam/shell section INP generation) would make each concern independently testable and easier to navigate. The orchestration and file-writing coordination stays in UnifiedCalculixWriter.

title: Fix mixed beam+shell instability: rotational zero-energy modes under lateral load
description: When B31 beam elements and shell elements are connected only via DOF 1-3 EQUATION constraints, and column bases are pinned (DOF 1-3 only from IfcBoundaryNodeCondition), the structure has rotational zero-energy modes under lateral load. building_01 demonstrates this: lateral forces on a pinned-base frame with no moment-resisting connections produce a near-mechanism. At minimum, the library should detect and warn about this condition rather than silently producing wrong results. The fix may involve upgrading shared beam+shell node connections to DOF 1-6 EQUATION constraints where appropriate.

title: Fix intermediate support positions being silently omitted
description: If a support connection is at an intermediate point on a beam (not at a beam endpoint), Gmsh may not place a mesh node at that exact location, causing the support to be silently omitted. The grid_of_beams example demonstrates this.

title: Add missing type annotations to private methods in meshing layer
description: 17+ private methods in unified_calculix_writer.py and gmsh_geometry.py lack parameter or return type annotations, reducing IDE support and making mypy unable to catch type errors in the most complex parts of the codebase. Key gaps: _extract_cell_blocks, _assign_elements_spatially, _distribute_elements_to_members, _write_list_in_chunks, _write_beam_section_for_set, _write_beam_section_general, _write_point_connection, _find_connection_nodes_at_location (all in unified_calculix_writer.py); _ensure_gmsh_initialized, _create_curve_geometry, _create_surface_geometry, apply_mesh_size, _create_rectangle_in_plane (in gmsh_geometry.py). At minimum, return types should be added; parameter types should follow.

title: Fix direct mutation of config._config dict in structural_analysis.py
description: api/structural_analysis.py lines 380 and 406 mutate the internal _config dict of AnalysisConfig directly (config._config['analysis_type'] = ..., config._config['solver_params'] = ...) instead of using setter methods. This bypasses any validation logic in the setter path and breaks encapsulation. The fix is to add setter methods to AnalysisConfig (or use keyword arguments at construction time) and remove the direct dict access.

title: Remove or document unused public methods in extraction and analysis layers
description: 16 public methods exist in src/ with no callers: extraction-layer APIs (extract_all_members, extract_all_connections, extract_connection_by_id, get_warnings, get_pset_property, get_pset_properties) that predate the unified Extractor.extract_model() approach; output_parser methods (classify_error_severity, map_error_to_entity, generate_error_summary) that appear superseded by ErrorDetector but retained without explanation; and calculix_runner getters (get_result_files, set_mapper, get_mapper) that are never called. Each should either be deleted (if truly dead), documented with a note explaining why it exists, or moved to a separate optional API surface.

value: Overlapping-geometry members (MeshMapper's shared-element-assignment fallback) can leave stale references: _identify_and_retype_u1_members() retypes shared elements to U1 in the global self.elements dict, but must also strip them from every non-U1 member's element_sets entry (added in fixing 51j) — otherwise a native *BEAM SECTION ELSET references elements that _write_elements() never writes (it explicitly skips U1-typed elements, deferring them to _write_sections()). Also, _write_sections()'s overlap dedup guard must SUBTRACT already-claimed elements and write a section for the remainder, not skip the whole member on any overlap — a member sharing only some elements with an earlier-processed member would otherwise lose ALL its elements. CalculiX's resulting error for the first bug is misleadingly generic: '*BEAM SECTION can only be used for beam elements. Element N is not a beam element' even though element N is actually just undefined anywhere in the file.
